$comment: Source of truth for the Awesome 3D Agents list. Edit here, then run `npm run build:awesome` to regenerate awesome/README.md and public/awesome.json. Every url is checked by `npm run awesome:links`.
title: Awesome 3D Agents
tagline: Everything you need to give an AI agent a body.
intro: A curated list of the models, engines, formats, and research that turn a language model into something you can see, animate, talk to, and put on a web page. Generation, rigging, motion, faces, voice, renderers, and the agent frameworks that drive them.

sections.title: Text and image to 3D
sections.description: Generate a mesh from a prompt or a single photo. This is the front door of the pipeline: the fastest way to get geometry that did not exist an hour ago.

items.name: TRELLIS
items.description: Structured latent generation that emits meshes, radiance fields, and Gaussians from the same model. Currently the strongest open text and image to 3D quality.

items.name: Hunyuan3D 2
items.description: Shape generation plus a separate texture synthesis stage, so the mesh and its material are not fighting for the same capacity. Ships usable PBR maps.

items.name: TripoSR
items.description: Single image to 3D in well under a second on one GPU. The reference point for fast feed-forward reconstruction.

items.name: InstantMesh
items.description: Multi-view diffusion into a large reconstruction model, tuned for clean topology rather than the blobby output that plagues earlier feed-forward work.

items.name: Stable Fast 3D
items.description: Image to UV-unwrapped, textured mesh in roughly half a second, with material parameter prediction built in.

items.name: LGM
items.description: Large multi-view Gaussian model. High-resolution 3D from text or a single image, then converted to a mesh.

items.name: Wonder3D
items.description: Cross-domain diffusion that generates consistent normal maps and colour views together, which is why its surfaces hold up under relighting.

items.name: CRM
items.description: Convolutional reconstruction model. Single image to a textured mesh in about ten seconds without per-object optimisation.

items.name: Zero-1-to-3
items.description: The novel-view-synthesis paper most of this section is built on. Learn what your favourite generator is actually doing by reading this one.

items.name: threestudio
items.description: One framework, many text-to-3D methods (DreamFusion, Magic3D, ProlificDreamer, and more) behind a shared config system. The right place to compare approaches honestly.

items.name: Shap-E
items.description: Generates implicit functions that render as both meshes and neural radiance fields. Old now, but small, permissive, and easy to run.

items.name: Point-E
items.description: Text to point cloud on a single GPU in a minute or two. Still the cheapest way to get rough 3D structure from a prompt.

items.name: three.ws Forge
items.description: A free hosted text-to-3D lane with no key and no account. Returns a GLB you can download, embed, or rig.

items.name: Meshy
items.description: Commercial text and image to 3D with quad remeshing and PBR texturing. Good API, generous enough free tier to evaluate properly.

items.name: Tripo
items.description: The hosted product from the TripoSR authors. Fast previews, refined high-poly output, and a documented API.

items.name: Rodin
items.description: Generation aimed at production assets: clean topology options, PBR materials, and part-level control.

sections.title: Photos and video to 3D
sections.description: Capture reality instead of inventing it. Photogrammetry, neural fields, and Gaussian splatting, plus the viewers that get the result onto the web.

items.name: 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.description: The original INRIA implementation that made radiance fields real-time. Everything in this section is downstream of it.

items.name: gsplat
items.description: A CUDA-accelerated splatting library with a clean Python API, faster and far less memory-hungry than the reference code.

items.name: Nerfstudio
items.description: A modular pipeline for neural radiance fields and splats, with a real-time web viewer and a sane data-processing story.

items.name: Spark
items.description: A Gaussian splatting renderer that drops into an existing three.js scene as ordinary objects, so splats and meshes light and sort together.

items.name: SuperSplat
items.description: A browser-based editor for cleaning, cropping, and compressing splat captures before you publish them.

items.name: Brush
items.description: A splatting engine in Rust and wgpu that trains and renders on the web, macOS, Linux, Windows, and Android from one codebase.

items.name: OpenSplat
items.description: Splat training on CPU as well as CUDA and Metal, which makes it the practical option on machines without an NVIDIA card.

items.name: COLMAP
items.description: Structure from motion and multi-view stereo. The camera poses almost every method above expects as input come from here.

items.name: DUSt3R
items.description: Dense 3D reconstruction from unconstrained image pairs with no camera calibration at all. It quietly deleted a whole preprocessing stage.

items.name: VGGT
items.description: A single feed-forward transformer that predicts camera poses, depth, and point maps together in seconds.

items.name: Meshroom
items.description: A node-graph photogrammetry application on top of AliceVision. The friendliest free path from a folder of photos to a textured mesh.

items.name: splat
items.description: A WebGL splat viewer in a few hundred readable lines. Read it once and you will understand the whole rendering technique.

items.name: Luma AI
items.description: Phone capture to a shareable splat, with an embed and a web SDK.

items.name: Polycam
items.description: LiDAR and photo capture on phones with mesh, splat, and glTF export. The fastest route from a real object to a file you can use.

sections.title: Avatars and characters
sections.description: Humanoid bodies that arrive already rigged, already skinned, and ready to be driven. Building one from scratch is rarely the right first move.

items.name: Avaturn
items.description: Photorealistic avatars from a phone photo, exported as GLB or FBX with a standard humanoid skeleton.

items.name: VRoid Studio
items.description: A free desktop editor for anime-style VRM characters, with hair, clothing, and expression authoring built in.

items.name: three-vrm
items.description: The VRM runtime for three.js: spring bones, look-at, expressions, and material handling that a plain glTF loader will not give you.

items.name: VRM specification
items.description: The glTF extension that standardises humanoid bones, expressions, look-at, and licence metadata. Read it before you invent your own avatar format.

items.name: MakeHuman
items.description: An open parametric human generator with a full skeleton and topology you can actually edit. Old-fashioned, and still unmatched for free anatomically-driven bodies.

items.name: SMPL-X
items.description: A parametric body model with articulated hands and an expressive face. The shared coordinate system that most human motion research speaks.

items.name: Character Creator
items.description: Commercial character authoring with production-grade topology, morphs, and direct export to game engines.

items.name: three.ws Avatar Studio
items.description: Generate, rig, dress, and pose an avatar in the browser, then embed it anywhere with one script tag.

sections.title: Rigging and retargeting
sections.description: A mesh without a skeleton is a statue. This is the layer that decides whether an avatar can be animated at all.

items.name: Mixamo
items.description: Free automatic humanoid rigging plus a large motion-capture library. Its bone naming has become an informal industry convention.

items.name: UniRig
items.description: An autoregressive model that rigs humans, animals, and objects from one checkpoint, predicting the skeleton and the skin weights together.

items.name: RigNet
items.description: The neural rigging paper this field grew out of: joint prediction, skeleton connectivity, and skinning learned end to end.

items.name: AccuRIG
items.description: A free desktop auto-rigger for static humanoid meshes, with clean weight painting and direct export to standard skeletons.

items.name: Rigify
items.description: Blender's bundled meta-rig system. Free, scriptable, and the practical fallback when an automatic rigger gets a character wrong.

items.name: SkeletonUtils
items.description: three.js retargeting helpers that map a clip authored for one skeleton onto another at runtime. Small, unglamorous, and load-bearing.

sections.title: Motion and animation
sections.description: Generated motion, captured motion, and the datasets both are trained on. A body that only idles is a prop.

items.name: Motion Diffusion Model
items.description: Text to human motion via a lightweight diffusion model. The reference implementation nearly every later method compares against.

items.name: MoMask
items.description: Generative masked modelling of motion tokens. Faster and sharper than diffusion baselines, with editing and in-betweening for free.

items.name: MotionGPT
items.description: Treats motion as a language, so one model generates, captions, predicts, and in-betweens with the same interface.

items.name: T2M-GPT
items.description: VQ-VAE plus a transformer for text-driven motion. A clean, readable codebase to learn the tokenised-motion approach from.

items.name: OmniControl
items.description: Adds spatial control signals to motion diffusion, so you can pin a hand to a location instead of hoping the prompt lands.

items.name: HumanML3D
items.description: The text-and-motion dataset behind most of this section. If you are benchmarking, you are benchmarking on this.

items.name: AMASS
items.description: Fifteen-plus motion capture datasets unified onto one SMPL body. The reason cross-dataset motion training is possible at all.

items.name: Cascadeur
items.description: Keyframe animation software with physics-aware assistance and AutoPosing, usable free for individuals under a revenue threshold.

items.name: Rokoko
items.description: Motion capture suits and a free video-to-motion tool, plus a Blender plugin that handles retargeting.

sections.title: Faces, lipsync, and voice
sections.description: The difference between a model standing there and an agent talking to you. Speech in, speech out, and a mouth that agrees with the audio.

items.name: TalkingHead
items.description: A three.js class that turns a glTF humanoid avatar into a talking head with visemes, gaze, and mood. The most complete open reference for this exact problem.

items.name: Rhubarb Lip Sync
items.description: Offline audio to mouth-shape timings as a plain command line tool. No model to host, no API to pay for.

items.name: MediaPipe
items.description: Face landmarks and blendshape coefficients in the browser at video rate, which is enough to drive an avatar's face from a webcam.

items.name: ARKit blendshapes
items.description: The 52-coefficient facial vocabulary that avatar formats, capture tools, and generators have all standardised on.

items.name: Whisper
items.description: Robust multilingual speech recognition that made self-hosted transcription the default rather than the exception.

items.name: faster-whisper
items.description: A CTranslate2 reimplementation of Whisper that is several times faster at the same accuracy. Use this in production, not the reference code.

items.name: whisper.cpp
items.description: Whisper in plain C and C++ with no dependencies, running on phones, browsers via WebAssembly, and Raspberry Pis.

items.name: Kokoro
items.description: An 82M-parameter text to speech model with quality that embarrasses far larger ones, small enough to run in a browser tab.

items.name: Piper
items.description: Fast local neural text to speech built for low-power devices, with a large set of pretrained voices.

items.name: F5-TTS
items.description: Flow-matching text to speech with convincing zero-shot voice cloning from a few seconds of reference audio.

items.name: Coqui TTS
items.description: A deep-learning toolkit covering dozens of text to speech and voice-conversion models, including XTTS multilingual cloning.

items.name: Silero VAD
items.description: Voice activity detection in under a millisecond per chunk. The unglamorous component that decides whether a voice agent feels responsive.

items.name: Pipecat
items.description: A Python framework for real-time voice and multimodal agents: pipelines, interruption handling, and transport out of the box.

items.name: LiveKit Agents
items.description: Build voice agents that join a WebRTC room, with turn detection and telephony handled for you.

items.name: Web Speech API
items.description: Recognition and synthesis already in the browser, with zero bytes shipped. Always check this before adding a model.

sections.title: Rendering on the web
sections.description: The runtime that actually puts the body on a page. Everything above is upstream of a choice made here.

items.name: three.js
items.description: The default WebGL and WebGPU library for the web, with the deepest ecosystem of loaders, controls, and examples anywhere.

items.name: React Three Fiber
items.description: three.js as a React renderer. Scene graphs become components, and the reconciler handles the mutation you would otherwise write by hand.

items.name: drei
items.description: The helper library that makes React Three Fiber practical: controls, loaders, staging, text, and effects you would otherwise rebuild every project.

items.name: Babylon.js
items.description: A batteries-included web engine with a built-in physics layer, node material editor, and an inspector that is genuinely better than the alternatives.

items.name: PlayCanvas
items.description: A lightweight engine tuned hard for load time and mobile, backed by a collaborative browser editor.

items.name: model-viewer
items.description: One custom element that renders a glTF with sensible defaults, accessibility, and AR on both phone platforms. The lowest-effort correct answer.

items.name: A-Frame
items.description: Declarative HTML for WebXR scenes, with an entity-component system underneath. Still the shortest path from markup to headset.

items.name: Threlte
items.description: three.js for Svelte, with a component library, physics bindings, and a preprocessor that keeps bundles small.

items.name: TresJS
items.description: three.js as Vue components, with reactivity mapped onto scene-graph updates.

items.name: OGL
items.description: A minimal WebGL library that stays close to the API instead of hiding it. The right tool when three.js is more engine than you need.

items.name: Needle Engine
items.description: Author in Unity or Blender, ship a small web build. A pragmatic bridge for teams whose content pipeline already exists.

items.name: agent-3d
items.description: A web component that drops a rigged, animated, lip-syncing agent avatar onto any page in one tag, with a JS API for moods and gestures.

sections.title: Formats and asset pipeline
sections.description: Getting the asset small, valid, and loadable. Most 3D-on-the-web failures are pipeline failures, not rendering failures.

items.name: glTF
items.description: The transmission format for 3D on the web, plus its extension registry. If you are choosing a format, this is the answer.

items.name: glTF-Transform
items.description: Read, edit, optimise, and validate glTF from Node or the CLI. Deduplicate, resize textures, weld, and compress in a scripted pipeline.

items.name: meshoptimizer
items.description: Vertex cache optimisation, simplification, and the meshopt compression that glTF files use. Its gltfpack CLI is the single highest-leverage step in most pipelines.

items.name: Draco
items.description: Geometry compression that shrinks meshes and point clouds hard, with decoders for the browser.

items.name: KTX-Software
items.description: Basis Universal texture transcoding. GPU-compressed textures that stay compressed in memory, which is usually the real budget problem.

items.name: glTF-Validator
items.description: Tells you whether a file is actually valid before a user's browser does. Wire it into CI and stop guessing.

items.name: glTF Sample Assets
items.description: The official test models, including deliberately awkward ones. Your loader is not done until these render correctly.

items.name: Blender
items.description: Free, scriptable in Python, and headless-capable, which makes it the workhorse of automated 3D pipelines as much as an authoring tool.

items.name: trimesh
items.description: The Python library for loading, repairing, measuring, and booleaning meshes. Nearly every 3D backend service has this in it somewhere.

items.name: Assimp
items.description: Imports roughly fifty 3D formats into one data structure. The escape hatch when someone sends you a file nothing else opens.

items.name: OpenUSD
items.description: Pixar's scene description for large, layered, collaboratively edited worlds. Heavier than glTF, and the right answer above a certain scale.

items.name: three-mesh-bvh
items.description: Bounding volume hierarchies for three.js geometry, turning raycasts against dense meshes from unusable into instant.

sections.title: Physics, networking, and shared worlds
sections.description: One avatar in a viewer is a demo. Several avatars in a place, with gravity and collisions, is a product.

items.name: Rapier
items.description: A Rust physics engine with deterministic cross-platform simulation and first-class WebAssembly bindings.

items.name: Jolt Physics
items.description: The multi-core physics engine used in shipped AAA titles, with a WebAssembly build that runs in the browser.

items.name: cannon-es
items.description: A maintained fork of cannon.js in modern JavaScript. Small and readable, and enough for character controllers and props.

items.name: Colyseus
items.description: Authoritative multiplayer rooms with automatic state synchronisation and delta encoding, in Node.

items.name: Yjs
items.description: CRDTs for shared editable state, with providers for WebRTC, WebSocket, and IndexedDB persistence.

items.name: LiveKit
items.description: An open WebRTC server for real-time audio and video, with SDKs everywhere and a self-hostable path.

items.name: mediasoup
items.description: A selective forwarding unit as a Node library rather than a service, for teams that want to own the media path.

items.name: geckos.io
items.description: Unreliable UDP-like messaging in the browser over WebRTC data channels, which is what fast-moving avatar positions actually want.

items.name: WebXR Device API
items.description: The specification behind every headset and phone AR session on the open web. Read the spec, not just a framework's wrapper.

sections.title: Agent frameworks and protocols
sections.description: The mind that drives the body. Listed here because embodiment is a rendering problem bolted onto an agent problem, and most teams underestimate the second one.

items.name: Model Context Protocol
items.description: The open protocol for giving a model tools, resources, and prompts from an external server. The cleanest way to let an agent act on a 3D pipeline.

items.name: Claude Agent SDK
items.description: Build agents on the same harness Claude Code runs on: tool loops, subagents, permissions, and session state.

items.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
items.description: A small framework for multi-agent handoffs, guardrails, and tracing, with a deliberately thin abstraction layer.

items.name: LangGraph
items.description: Agents as explicit stateful graphs, with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop pauses. The right shape when a flow must be resumable.

items.name: Vercel AI SDK
items.description: One TypeScript interface across model providers, with streaming, structured output, and tool calls that work in the browser.

items.name: smolagents
items.description: Agents that write Python to call their tools instead of emitting JSON, in about a thousand lines of library code.

items.name: CrewAI
items.description: Role-based multi-agent orchestration with an emphasis on readable task delegation.

items.name: AutoGen
items.description: A research-grade framework for conversational multi-agent systems, with an event-driven core and a visual builder.

items.name: Mastra
items.description: A TypeScript agent framework with workflows, memory, and evals, aimed at shipping rather than research.

items.name: Letta
items.description: Agents with persistent memory as a first-class server concept, out of the MemGPT research line.

items.name: A2A
items.description: An open protocol for agents built by different vendors to discover each other and collaborate over a common envelope.

items.name: Generative Agents
items.description: The Stanford simulation where twenty-five agents with memory, reflection, and planning produced emergent social behaviour. Still the clearest demonstration of why memory architecture matters.

items.name: Voyager
items.description: An embodied agent that plays Minecraft by writing and saving its own skills as code, then composing them. The best existing argument for embodiment as a learning signal.

sections.title: Datasets and simulators
sections.description: What the models in this list were trained and evaluated on, and where embodied agents go to practise.

items.name: Objaverse
items.description: Around 800,000 annotated 3D objects, and the XL release pushes past ten million. The dataset that made open 3D generation viable.

items.name: Objaverse-XL
items.description: The download and processing tooling for the ten-million-object release, including deduplication and rendering scripts.

items.name: ShapeNet
items.description: The categorised CAD-model dataset that anchored 3D deep learning for a decade, mirrored on Hugging Face while its original site is unreliable.

items.name: Habitat
items.description: A fast photorealistic simulator for training embodied agents to navigate and manipulate in indoor scenes.

items.name: AI2-THOR
items.description: Interactive 3D rooms where objects have state: doors open, eggs break, appliances turn on. Built for agents that change the world rather than tour it.

items.name: BEHAVIOR
items.description: A benchmark of a thousand everyday household activities defined in a logic language, with simulated physics and states.

items.name: ScanNet
items.description: Richly annotated RGB-D scans of real indoor spaces, and the benchmark most scene-understanding work still reports on.

sections.title: Free assets
sections.description: Models, textures, and lighting you can ship without a lawyer. Every project in this list looks better with a real HDRI behind it.

items.name: Poly Haven
items.description: HDRIs, PBR textures, and models, all CC0, all high quality, with no account required. Start here.

items.name: ambientCG
items.description: Thousands of CC0 PBR material sets at multiple resolutions, downloadable in bulk.

items.name: Kenney
items.description: Tens of thousands of CC0 game assets, including clean low-poly 3D kits that prototype beautifully.

items.name: Quaternius
items.description: Stylised CC0 model packs with consistent proportions across sets, so a scene assembled from several packs still looks intentional.

items.name: Sketchfab
items.description: The largest 3D model library on the web, with a downloadable Creative Commons subset and glTF export.

items.name: OpenGameArt
items.description: A long-running community archive of openly licensed art. Uneven, and it holds things that exist nowhere else.

sections.title: Learning
sections.description: How to get good at this. Read in roughly this order.

items.name: three.js manual
items.description: The official guide, rewritten around real problems rather than API surface. The fastest correct start.

items.name: Discover three.js
items.description: A free book that teaches the concepts underneath the library, including colour management and performance work most tutorials skip.

items.name: Three.js Journey
items.description: Bruno Simon's paid course, and the most thorough path from nothing to shaders and production scenes.

items.name: The Book of Shaders
items.description: An interactive introduction to fragment shaders. Work through it once and materials stop being magic.

items.name: WebGL Fundamentals
items.description: What every abstraction in this list is hiding, explained from first principles with runnable examples.

items.name: WebGPU Fundamentals
items.description: The same treatment for WebGPU, which is where the web's rendering stack is heading.

items.name: Real-Time Rendering resources
items.description: The companion site to the standard reference text, with a maintained portal into graphics literature.
